issues.title: Changed public CSS/JS have no cache-busting, and stale-while-revalidate=7d serves old JS with new HTML
issues.file: vercel.json:17-21; index.html:15,18-20; activities.html:13,17-20; gallery.html:11,13-16; knowledge.html; halal-map.html; about.html
issues.description: Public pages load assets/mccmu.css, assets/api.js, assets/site.js and assets/i18n.js without ?v=, and all four changed in this deploy. HTML is max-age=0, so a returning visitor gets the new HTML at once. Assets are 'public, max-age=600, stale-while-revalidate=604800', so any copy cached in the last 7 days + 10 minutes is served stale (revalidated in the background) on the first load after deploy. That is more than the 10-minute window the brief assumes. The new HTML has dropped markup the old api.js needs (#lb lightbox, #galPrev/#galNext, the inline prayer script), and the old api.js has no 'gallery' case.
reproduction_steps: In a fresh window on :8908, write the new /activities HTML but load api.js and mccmu.css from production (identical to HEAD); click an album
Same for new /gallery HTML and new / HTML
issues.user_impact: For each returning visitor's first page view after deploy: on /activities, clicking an album throws a TypeError and no viewer opens. /gallery shows an empty grid with no message (0 children). On the home page the prayer strip renders as 5 unstyled stacked divs in a decimal <ol> (318px tall), with no Hijri date and no 'next prayer' line. A reload fixes it, but the user isn't told that.
issues.recommended_fix: Add the same ?v=YYYYMMDDx scheme used in admin/index.html to every public <link>/<script> for mccmu.css, api.js, site.js, i18n.js and the new gallery/videos files, and bump it on each deploy. Alternatively, drop stale-while-revalidate for /assets/*.css|js in vercel.json, or make it short (e.g. 60s).

issues.title: Production publicly serves internal docs, DB migrations, seed SQL, data backups, scripts and a test page
issues.description: There is no .vercelignore and the Vercel project serves the repo root, so every tracked file is public. Verified with GET on production: ADMIN_SETUP.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, MIGRATION-VERCEL.md, .mcp.json (Supabase project ref and MCP config), .github/workflows/backup-data.yml, backend/Code.gs and *.md plans, supabase/migrations/*.sql (full schema and RLS policies), supabase/seed/*.sql, data/backup/*.json (all tables incl. members/settings), scripts/*.sh|py and drive-image-test.html (a dev test page at /drive-image-test). No secret values were found in them, but this is internal information and a map for attackers. The untracked .claude/ (agent prompts, audit brief, admin-mock.html, devserver.mjs, launch.json), data/import/, data/review/ and supabase/seed/halal-restaurants-2026-10-13.sql are not in .gitignore, so a 'git add -A' would publish them too.
reproduction_steps: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://mccmuclub.vercel.app/ADMIN_SETUP.md (and the paths listed in evidence)
issues.user_impact: Anyone can download the DB schema and RLS rules, admin setup procedure, MCP config, internal plans and full nightly data dumps. After a careless 'git add -A', the AI-agent prompts, the audit tooling and the unverified restaurant review notes would also be public.
issues.recommended_fix: Add a .vercelignore that excludes *.md, .mcp.json, .github/, .claude/, backend/, data/, supabase/, scripts/, drive-image-test.html, uploads/ and screenshots/. Add .claude/ (or at least .claude/audit/), data/import/ and data/review/ to .gitignore, or commit them deliberately. Then re-check with curl -I that they return 404.

issues.title: Nightly backup workflow still copies the abandoned Google Sheet and makes a no-op prod deploy daily
issues.description: Production reads Supabase (/data source:'supabase'), but the nightly 'Backup data' workflow still pulls from Google Sheets via Apps Script (_meta.json source 'google-sheets-via-apps-script'). The data no longer changes there, so the job commits only the new generated_at timestamp every night. Each push to main triggers a Vercel production deploy. Local main is now 41 commits behind origin/main because of these bot commits.
reproduction_steps: git log HEAD..origin/main --format=%an | sort | uniq -c -> 41 github-actions[bot]
git diff --stat HEAD origin/main -> only data/backup/_meta.json, 1 line
Compare counts: _meta.json places=18, members=18 vs prod /data?sheet=all places=29, members=23
issues.user_impact: The 'backup' doesn't contain the live Supabase data (e.g. today's 11 restaurants, new members), so it can't restore the site. There are 41 needless production deploys, and the next 'git push' of this release is rejected until main is pulled or rebased.
issues.recommended_fix: Before pushing, run git pull --rebase (bot commits only touch data/backup/_meta.json, so no conflict is expected). Then point scripts/backup-data.sh at Supabase (anon REST, published rows) or retire the workflow, and make it skip committing when only generated_at changed.

issues.title: DATA_SOURCE falls back to the retired Google Sheets backend when unset
issues.description: DEFAULT_SOURCE = (process.env.DATA_SOURCE || 'sheets'). With the variable missing (e.g. a Preview-scoped env, a new Vercel project or a typo), /data serves 200 OK from the stale Google Sheet with no error, so a misconfiguration goes unnoticed. ?src=sheets also lets anyone force the stale source in production. Production currently has DATA_SOURCE=supabase set.
reproduction_steps: Run the handler with env vars unset: node run-handler.mjs data.mjs '/data?sheet=settings' -> 200 with Sheets data
issues.user_impact: On a misconfigured deployment, visitors silently see out-of-date content (e.g. 18 instead of 29 places) and admin edits seem to have no effect.
issues.recommended_fix: Default to 'supabase' now that the migration is done (or fail loudly with 500 when DATA_SOURCE is missing). Consider ignoring ?src= unless an explicit debug env flag is set.
issues.evidence: Local run with all env unset: '/data?sheet=settings -> 200 public, max-age=120, s-maxage=180 ... {"ok":true,"data":{"logo_id":"","club_email":""...' (Apps Script response).

issues.title: Admin imports supabase-js from a floating major-version CDN URL
issues.description: import { createClient } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@supabase/supabase-js@2/+esm' resolves to whatever 2.x is latest at load time. A new minor release can change admin behaviour without any deploy, which makes production non-reproducible.
issues.user_impact: Admin login or CRUD could break unexpectedly after an upstream release, with no code change to roll back.
issues.recommended_fix: Pin an exact version, e.g. @supabase/supabase-js@2.x.y/+esm, and optionally add SRI or self-host it.

issues.title: No custom 404 page; unknown URLs show Vercel's plain-text NOT_FOUND
issues.description: There is no 404.html, so mistyped or old links (e.g. the /gallery link before it deploys, or old club.mccmu.workers.dev paths) land on Vercel's bare text page with no navigation back to the site.
issues.user_impact: Visitors who follow a bad link reach a dead end.
issues.recommended_fix: Add a branded 404.html at the repo root, using site.js nav and a link home. Vercel serves it automatically.

notes.text: Preview mode is sticky per tab (sessionStorage mccmu_preview). Opening any ?preview URL without an admin session makes every later page in that tab log '[MCCMU] settings/featured/picks/prayer/past carousel: Error: preview: no admin session', and the data sections stay empty. Seen on :8908 / and on the next /activities load.

gallery.html has no window.MCCMU_SUPABASE inline config (the other 5 public pages have it), so assets/site.js visit tracking returns early and /gallery views are never counted, although admin.js:472 labels '/gallery' in stats.
gallery.html lacks the apple-touch-icon and dns-prefetch links that the other public pages have.
Internal nav links use href='x.html', so with cleanUrls every click costs an extra 308 redirect hop (e.g. activities.html -> /activities).
vercel.json sets no security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy). Prod only returns HSTS.

/data responses send access-control-allow-origin: * (api/data.js:49,64), which conflicts with the project rule 'Restrict CORS to trusted domains'. Preview responses are no-store, but CORS is still wildcard.

The preview tool was capped at 5 servers (held by other auditors), so I ran the same devserver command (node .claude/audit/devserver.mjs . 8908) as a background shell job on my assigned port 8908, and stopped it at the end.
